get.description: The built-in crops a profile can start from, each with its usual growth stages, named in en, fa and ar. The library sets no target values: those depend on the variety, the cultivation system and the site.
The crops this workspace product grows, oldest first. Archived ones only with includeArchived.

post.description: From the library (templateKey) or custom (a name). Made from the library with no stages listed, it takes the library's stages with no targets set. A stage sent with a library stage's key as its id keeps that stage's names in every language; one without an id is a new stage of the grower's own and needs a name. A target bounds one measurement (TEMPERATURE in °C, HUMIDITY in %, VPD in kPa, CO2 in ppm, DLI in mol/m²/d, SUBSTRATE_MOISTURE in %, PH, EC in mS/cm) by DAY, NIGHT or ALL.

stages.name: Topping
stages.irrigation: Cut back as the last trusses set

put.description: Replaces everything but the library crop it came from. With stages left out the stages stay as they are. A stage a growing crop cycle is in cannot be removed.

stages.name: Topping
stages.irrigation: Cut back as the last trusses set

400.description: Invalid field, or removes a stage in use

delete.description: A crop no cycle has grown is deleted. One with crop cycles is archived instead, so their history stays; no new cycle starts with it.

get.description: Newest planting first. Filter by status, the zone or bed, the greenhouse, or the crop.

post.description: Plants a crop in a zone or growing bed. A zone or bed grows one crop at a time: start another there once the one growing is completed or archived. The cycle starts in the stage given, or the crop's first.

400.description: Not a zone or bed, archived crop, or unknown stage

409.description: Something is already growing there

get.description: With the stage it is in and that stage's targets.

put.description: Its variety, planting date, expected harvest and notes. The stage changes through /stage.

400.description: Invalid field, or the cycle is archived

get.description: Oldest first: STARTED, STAGE, OBSERVATION, HARVEST, COMPLETED, ARCHIVED.

post.description: Moves a growing cycle to another of its crop's stages, from occurredAt (default now). The stage's targets then apply. A cycle never changes stage by itself.

400.description: Not growing, same stage, or unknown stage
Empty note, or the cycle is archived

post.description: How much was picked, in the unit the grower counts in (kg, crates, heads...).

400.description: Invalid quantity, or the cycle is archived

post.description: The crop is done; the zone or bed is free for the next one. Harvests can still be recorded on it.
Closes it for good, keeping its history; for a finished cycle, or one that was given up.

get.description: Every greenhouse of the location tree, by name, with its details, its zones and their growing beds, the crop cycle growing in each, and how many devices are placed on it. Greenhouses, zones and beds themselves are created and renamed through the asset tree (types GREENHOUSE, ZONE, BED).

get.summary: Get a greenhouse's or zone's details

put.summary: Set a greenhouse's or zone's details
put.description: Replaces them; a field left out is cleared. For a zone only the area is shown.

400.description: Not a greenhouse or zone, or an unknown value

put.description: Stores the panel colour on the account, so it follows the user to every device. panelAccent is "paapeli" or "green"; null returns to the brand's own colour. GET /users/me reads it back.

Changes the password, or sets the first one of an account made by Google sign-in (then currentPassword may be omitted; see hasPassword on GET /users/me). A new password has 8 characters at least and 72 UTF-8 bytes at most. Every session, this one included, is signed out after.

post.description: Creates a new authenticator secret (TOTP: SHA-1, six digits, 30 seconds). otpauthUri is what the QR code holds; secret is the same key to type in. It counts only once /enable proves it with a code.

409.description: TWO_FACTOR_ALREADY_ON

post.description: A current code from the authenticator turns two-factor on. The answer lists ten one-time recovery codes, shown this once. From then on, password and Google sign-in end in a challenge (POST /auth/login/two-factor).

409.description: TWO_FACTOR_ALREADY_ON or TWO_FACTOR_NOT_SET_UP

post.description: Ten new recovery codes for a current authenticator or recovery code; the old ones stop working.

409.description: TWO_FACTOR_OFF

post.description: Needs a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code. The secret and recovery codes are dropped.

409.description: TWO_FACTOR_OFF

put.description: Saves an address other than the account's own and emails it a six-digit code, good for ten minutes and five tries; another may be asked for after 60 seconds. Once confirmed, password reset codes go to it as well.

post.description: The emailed code verifies the recovery email. A wrong code is CODE_INVALID with attemptsLeft.

get.description: How many active members the workspace has and how many sign in with two-factor, with the password rule every account is held to. Any member with workspace READ access may read it.

post.summary: Finish signing in with the second factor
post.description: For an account with two-factor on, POST /auth/login and POST /auth/google answer {"twoFactorRequired": true, "challengeToken": "..."} instead of a token. Send that token here with a current authenticator code or an unused recovery code to get the session (token and refresh cookie). The challenge lasts five minutes and five wrong codes.

put.description:
Sets the name shown for the user across the panel and to the
members of their workspaces. It is trimmed and may be at most
100 characters; a blank or null name clears it, and the email
stands in.

post.summary: Text a verification code to my phone
post.description:
Sends a six-digit code to the saved phone, which must be an
Iranian mobile (+989...). The code is good for two minutes
and five tries. A new code may be asked for 60 seconds after
the last, and a number gets at most five codes an hour. Only
a verified number is ever sent an alarm.

A refusal is a problem response whose code says why:
PHONE_NOT_SET and ALREADY_VERIFIED (409), UNSUPPORTED_NUMBER
(400), RESEND_TOO_SOON and HOURLY_LIMIT (429, with
retryAfterSeconds), SMS_UNAVAILABLE (503).

sandboxCode carries the code itself only in test mode,
where no text message is actually sent.

409.description: No phone saved, or it is already verified

429.description: Asked again too soon, or five codes this hour

503.description: Text messages are not available right now

post.summary: Confirm my phone with the texted code
post.description:
A right code marks the phone verified. A wrong one is a 400
with code CODE_INVALID and attemptsLeft; the fifth wrong one
spends the code (429, TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS). An expired code, or
one sent to a number since changed, is CODE_EXPIRED; no code
at all is NO_PENDING_CODE.

409.description: No phone saved

get.description:
How many alarm texts the workspace has sent today and in the
last 30 days, across all its products, with the limits they
are held to. A text goes only to a verified phone, at most
once per member, rule and device in cooldownMinutes, and no
more than dailyLimit a day for the workspace; past that,
escalations reach people in the panel and owners and admins
are told once. "Today" starts at midnight Asia/Tehran.

put.description:
Creates or replaces the authenticated user's phone contact.
The phone number must use E.164 format, including the leading +.

Updates the label, description, provisioning profile,
and enabled state. The deviceType path key is
immutable. Profile changes affect future device
registrations only. Platform-administrator access
is required.

example.label: ZX909/C09 GPS tracker
example.description: GPS tracker using the ZX909/C09 protocol family

delete.description:
Deletes an unused device-type definition. Deletion
is rejected while the type is referenced by another
domain entity. Platform-administrator access is
required.

409.description: Device type is in use

put.description:
Updates command metadata, parameter schema, internal
dispatch configuration, and enabled state. The command
key is immutable. Changes apply to future command
requests only. Platform-administrator access is
required.

example.label: Set tracker location interval
example.description: Changes the tracker location reporting interval

delete.description:
Deletes an unused command definition. Platform-
administrator access is required.

409.description: Command is in use

put.description:
Adds an idempotent immediate parent-child rule. The same child
type may be allowed beneath multiple parent types, and
self-relations are valid. The rule is enforced when new
assets are reserved. Platform-administrator access is
required.

404.description: Parent or child type not found

409.description: ROOT cannot be used as a child type

delete.description:
Removes the rule for future asset creation. Existing assets
are not moved or invalidated. Platform-administrator access
is required.

put.description:
Updates the human-readable label and description. The
assetType path key is immutable. ROOT cannot be changed.
Platform-administrator access is required.

409.description: ROOT cannot be changed

delete.description:
Deletes an unused catalog entry. Deletion is rejected while
the type is used by a workspace asset or any allowed-child
rule. ROOT cannot be deleted. Platform-administrator access
is required.

409.description: Type is in use or ROOT was requested

put.description:
Updates the device name, label, and description. The request's
id selects the device. Device type, profile, asset assignment,
gateway flag, and credentials are preserved.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

409.description: The new device name conflicts

post.description:
Creates a device and assigns it to an active Paapeli asset
in the authorized workspace product. The supplied type must
be an enabled entry in the product device-type catalog.
Paapeli selects the provisioning profile internally; callers
cannot supply a profile identifier. For
ACCESS_TOKEN credentials, credentialValue may be omitted and
an identifier is generated.

MQTT basic device.value:
{
  "label": "Packaging gateway",
  "type": "gateway",
  "name": "packaging-gateway-01",
  "description": "Gateway for the packaging line",
  "isGateway": true,
  "credentialType": "MQTT_BASIC",
  "credentialValue": "{"clientId":"packaging-gateway-01","userName":"gateway","password":"replace-me"}",
  "assetId": "e75b06a5-a437-467a-b40b-2d31f0746056"
}

400.description: Invalid fields, profile, credentials, or conflicting device name

403.description: ADMINISTER access required or the asset is outside this workspace product

409.description: Device type is disabled or the target asset is not active

500.description: The configured provisioning profile is unavailable

404.description: Device type does not exist for the product

409.description: The device type does not support zones

put.summary: Create or replace a device zone
put.description:
Configures one circle, rectangle, or polygon for a
zone-capable device. Replaces the existing zone when one

409.description: The device type does not support zones

delete.description: Removes the configured zone from the device.

409.description: The device type does not support zones

get.description:
Returns the device's current authentication material.
ADMINISTER access is required because the response may expose
an access token, certificate, or password-bearing payload.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

put.description:
Replaces the authentication material for a device that belongs
to the authorized workspace product. ADMINISTER access is
required. Credential values are secrets: do not log or persist
the response in an insecure client store.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

put.description:
Updates an asset's name, label, and description. Its type and
parent cannot be changed. The system ROOT node is immutable.

403.description: ADMINISTER access required or ROOT was requested

409.description: Asset is not active or the new name conflicts

delete.description:
Deletes an active non-ROOT asset. The asset must have no child
assets and no assigned devices; callers should remove those
relationships first.

403.description: ADMINISTER access required or ROOT was requested

409.description: Asset is not active or is not empty

get.description:
Returns the configured escalation chain for an alarm rule,
preserving step and action order.

404.description: Alarm rule or escalation chain not found

put.summary: Create or replace an alarm escalation chain
put.description:
Creates or replaces the escalation chain for an active alarm rule.
Steps and actions execute in the order supplied. delaySeconds is the
wait before executing that step. Each action targets an active member
of the same workspace. Replacing a chain is atomic.

delete.description:
Deletes the escalation chain for an alarm rule. The operation is
idempotent when the alarm rule exists but has no escalation chain.

204.description: Escalation chain deleted or already absent

get.description: Lists workspaces in which the authenticated user has an ACTIVE membership.

403.description: An active user account is required

post.description:
Creates an active workspace. The authenticated user becomes
its active OWNER. Product infrastructure is not provisioned
until the workspace subscribes to a product.

403.description: An active user account is required

get.description: Lists the workspace's product subscriptions and their current states.

403.description: The caller cannot read this workspace

post.summary: Subscribe a workspace to a product
post.description:
Provisions the product's backing resources for the workspace
and activates the subscription. Only a role with
SUBSCRIBE_PRODUCT permission may call this endpoint. A failed
subscription can be retried; active, provisioning, and
suspended subscriptions conflict with a new request.

403.description: The caller cannot subscribe products for this workspace

409.description: Subscription or backing-resource provisioning conflicts with the current state

500.description: Provisioning failed; the response includes a reference ID

post.description:
Invites an existing active Paapeli user by email. OWNER cannot
be granted through an invitation. Workspace authorization
determines whether the caller may invite an ADMIN or a
MEMBER/VIEWER. A previously rejected or expired invitation
may be issued again.

400.description: Invalid role, self-invitation, or invitation state

403.description: The caller cannot invite this role

404.description: No active user exists with the supplied email

post.description: Rejects the authenticated user's pending invitation to the workspace.

403.description: An active user account is required

404.description: No pending invitation exists for this user and workspace

post.description: Accepts the authenticated user's pending invitation to the workspace.

403.description: An active user account is required

404.description: No pending invitation exists for this user and workspace

post.description:
Creates an active Paapeli user and returns an authentication
token. The email is normalized before uniqueness is checked.
Password and confirmedPassword must match, and each password
value may contain at most 72 UTF-8 bytes.

400.description: Validation failed or passwords do not match

409.description: An account with the normalized email already exists

post.description:
Replaces the password associated with a valid, unexpired,
one-time reset code. Submitting a code consumes it before the
password update is attempted, so a failed attempt requires a
new code. A successful reset also revokes previously issued
Paapeli access tokens for the account.

200.description: Password changed and previous access tokens revoked

400.description: Validation failed, passwords differ, or the code expired

404.description: The reset code is invalid or has already been used

post.description:
Requests a one-time password reset code for an active account.
The response is deliberately identical when the account does
not exist, is inactive, or the request is throttled. Repeated
requests for the same normalized email are limited by the
configured reset-request cooldown.

200.description: Generic response returned for every valid email-shaped request

example.message: If the account exists, a password reset email will be sent

400.description: The request body contains a malformed email

get.description: Lists all product definitions available for workspace subscription.

post.description:
Creates a global product definition and its system-managed
ROOT asset type. This is a Paapeli
platform-administrator operation; it does not subscribe a
workspace to the product.

409.description: The product key already exists

get.description:
Lists the product's device-type catalog. Disabled
entries remain visible but cannot be selected when
registering new devices.

post.description:
Adds an immutable device-type key to the product
catalog. Its label, description, provisioning
profile, and enabled state may be changed later.
Platform-administrator access is required.

example.label: ZX909 GPS tracker
example.description: GPS tracker using the ZX909 protocol family

409.description: Device type already exists

get.summary: List commands for a device type
get.description:
Lists the command catalog for the supplied product
device type. Disabled definitions remain visible but
cannot be selected for new command dispatches.
Internal dispatch configuration is not returned.

post.description:
Adds a command definition to a product device type.
The command key is immutable. Dispatch configuration
is used internally and is not included in the public
command representation. Platform-administrator access
is required.

example.label: Set location interval
example.description: Changes how frequently the tracker reports its location

409.description: Command already exists

get.description:
Lists the product's complete asset-type catalog, including
the system ROOT type. This endpoint lists definitions; use
the allowed-children endpoint to discover topology rules.

post.description:
Adds an immutable asset-type key to the product catalog.
The label and description may be changed later. ROOT is
system-managed and cannot be created through this endpoint.
Platform-administrator access is required.

409.description: Asset type already exists or ROOT was requested

post.summary: Send a command to a device
post.description:
Sends an enabled command from the device's command
catalog. Dispatch behavior is controlled by the
platform and cannot be overridden by callers.

A successful result confirms successful dispatch.
It does not necessarily confirm execution by the
physical device.

Reads and rotates the HttpOnly refresh-token cookie, then returns
a new access token. Browser clients calling from
`https://panel.paapeli.com` must use `credentials: "include"`
(Axios: `withCredentials: true`). Do not send the refresh token
in the request body or an Authorization header.
Revokes the current refresh-token family and clears its cookie.
Revokes every refresh-token family belonging to the authenticated user.

Authenticates an active Paapeli user by email and password.
Email matching is case-insensitive.

The JSON response contains the short-lived access token. Use it
as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on protected endpoints. The
refresh token is not exposed to JavaScript or returned in the
response body; it is stored in the `paapeli_refresh_token`
HttpOnly, Secure cookie.

Because the UI (`https://panel.paapeli.com`) and API
(`https://api.paapeli.com`) have different origins, browser
clients must opt into cookies on login, refresh, and logout:

```javascript
const login = await fetch(
  "https://api.paapeli.com/api/v1/aiot/auth/login",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    credentials: "include",
    body: JSON.stringify({ username, password })
  }
);
const { token } = await login.json();
```

When the access token expires, obtain a replacement by calling
`POST https://api.paapeli.com/api/v1/aiot/auth/refresh` with no
request body or Authorization header, but with
`credentials: "include"` (Axios: `withCredentials: true`). The
endpoint returns a new access token and rotates the refresh-token
cookie. A `401` response means the user must sign in again.

200.description: Authentication succeeded; the refresh token is set as an HttpOnly cookie

Set-Cookie.description: Rotating refresh token. Browser code must not read or persist this value.

schema.example: paapeli_refresh_token=<opaque>; Path=/api/v1/aiot/auth; Max-Age=2592000; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

post.description:
Verifies a Google ID token and returns a Paapeli bearer token.
A new active account is created when the verified Google email
is unknown. An existing password account with the same verified
email is linked to that Google identity.

401.description: Google token is invalid or the account is not active

get.description:
Returns one page of immediate children. It does not recursively
traverse descendants. Use hasChildren on each result to decide
whether the UI should request another level.

parameters.name: parentAssetId
parameters.description: Paapeli ID of the parent asset

post.description:
Creates a direct child beneath an active parent. The requested
type must be allowed beneath the parent's type by the product
catalog. That rule is enforced atomically while the local
asset is reserved, before external provisioning begins.

parameters.name: parentAssetId
parameters.description: Paapeli ID of the direct parent asset

409.description: Parent is not active, name conflicts, or the type is not allowed

get.description: Returns the active ROOT node used to start lazy loading the tree.

404.description: The asset-tree root has not been provisioned

409.description: The root exists but is not active

post.description:
Creates the workspace product's single system ROOT asset.
The product subscription must be active and the caller must
have ADMINISTER access. The ROOT node cannot later be edited
or deleted.

409.description: Root already exists or the workspace product is not ready

get.description:
Returns the local alarm-rule projection for a device in the authorized
workspace product, including provisioning and failed rules. Page numbers
are one-based and the requested page size is clamped to 1-100. The ID in
each item is the stable Paapeli alarm-rule ID accepted by the delete API.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Requested page size. Values are clamped to the range 1-100.

data.name: Sustained high temperature
data.description: Creates a major alarm after five minutes above the threshold

403.description: ADMINISTER product access required or device access denied

post.description:
Creates an alarm rule for a device in the authorized workspace product.
Each create rule is keyed by alarm severity. SIMPLE rules fire as soon as
their expression is true; DURATION rules require a positive duration and
time unit; REPEATING rules require a positive consecutive-event count.
Expressions may combine leaf rules with AND or OR. Literal values must use
the JSON type declared by valueType. An optional clearRule automatically
clears an active alarm when its expression becomes true.

simple.summary: Simple range rule with a clear condition

value.name: High temperature
value.description: Creates a critical alarm while temperature is between 50 and 200

value.name: Sustained high temperature
value.description: Creates a major alarm after five minutes above the threshold

value.name: Repeated overheating
value.description: Creates a warning after three consecutive threshold violations

403.description: ADMINISTER product access required or device access denied

post.description:
Clears an alarm associated with the specified device and records an
ALARM_CLEARED entry in the device activity timeline. The response
contains the alarm's updated state.

parameters.name: alarmId
parameters.description: Alarm ID returned by the alarm list endpoint

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Paapeli device ID associated with the alarm

400.description: Alarm is already cleared or cannot be cleared

403.description: OPERATE product access required, device access denied, or alarm does not belong to the device

post.description:
Acknowledges an alarm associated with the specified device and records an
ALARM_ACKNOWLEDGED entry in the device activity timeline. Acknowledgement
indicates that an operator has seen the alarm.

parameters.name: alarmId
parameters.description: Alarm ID returned by the alarm list endpoint

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Paapeli device ID associated with the alarm

400.description: Alarm is already acknowledged or cannot be acknowledged

403.description: OPERATE product access required, device access denied, or alarm does not belong to the device

get.description: Lists INVITED workspace memberships for the authenticated user.

403.description: An active user account is required

get.description:
Returns every available telemetry key for the device over a
recent lookback window. Despite its historical name, the
`from` parameter is a number of hours, not a timestamp. Values
are clamped to the supported range of 1 through 24 hours. Each
series contains at most 100 points in ascending timestamp order.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Lookback window in hours; clamped to 1-24

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

get.description: Lists the catalog types that may be created directly beneath the supplied parent type.
Lists all devices in the authorized workspace product, one page at a time.
Returns the Paapeli projection of a device in the authorized workspace product.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

delete.description:
Deletes a device that belongs to the authorized workspace
product, removes its local projection, and records a
DEVICE_DELETED activity.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

get.summary: List devices assigned to an asset
get.description: Lists devices assigned directly to the supplied Paapeli asset; child assets are not traversed.

Returns the device's Paapeli activity timeline. It includes
gateway lifecycle and command events, plus projected device
connectivity and alarm events such as DEVICE_ACTIVATED,
DEVICE_INACTIVATED, and ALARM_TRIGGERED. Newest activities
are returned first.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

get.summary: List types allowed beneath an asset
get.description:
Resolves the actual parent asset and returns the product types
permitted directly beneath it. This is the preferred endpoint
for populating the type selector in an asset-creation UI.

parameters.name: parentAssetId
parameters.description: Paapeli ID of the parent asset

get.description:
Returns the locally recorded alarms for every device in the
authorized workspace product. Current status is derived from
ALARM_TRIGGERED, ALARM_ACKNOWLEDGED, and ALARM_CLEARED
activities. acknowledgedAt and clearedAt are the times of the
first recorded ALARM_ACKNOWLEDGED and ALARM_CLEARED, and are
null when none was recorded, even if the reported status
says otherwise. Assignment is reserved in the
response and is null until alarm assignment is implemented.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Requested page size. Values are clamped to the range 1-100.

get.description:
Aggregates the alarms the authorized workspace product raised
in [from, to): totals, MTTA and MTTR, a timeline split by
severity, counts by severity, and the locations, devices and
rules raising the most alarms. openAlarms ignores the window
and covers every alarm not cleared yet, grouped by age.
Everything is computed in the database from local alarm
activities, so the response size does not grow with the
number of alarms.

from defaults to seven days before to, and to defaults to
now; the window may span at most 366 days. The timeline is
bucketed by hour up to three days, by day up to 92 days, and
by ISO week beyond that, with bucket boundaries in timeZone.
Empty buckets are included as zero. MTTA and MTTR average
only alarms with a recorded acknowledgement or clear, and
are null when there are none. Severity keys are
CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, WARNING and INDETERMINATE.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive window start, ISO-8601. Defaults to seven days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive window end, ISO-8601. Defaults to now.

parameters.name: timeZone
parameters.description: IANA time zone for timeline bucket boundaries. Defaults to UTC.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows in each top list, clamped to 1 through 50. Defaults to 10.

400.description: Malformed parameters, from not before to, a window over 366 days, or an unknown time zone

get.description:
Returns the local alarm-rule projection for the authorized
workspace product. Results include rules that are still
provisioning or have failed, and can optionally be filtered
by device.

Returns alarms for a device that belongs to the authorized
workspace product. Alarm creation is also projected into the
device activity timeline as ALARM_TRIGGERED when the alarm
originated from a device.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Requested page size. Values are clamped to the range 1-100.

404.description: Device not found in this workspace product

put.description:
Replaces an active alarm rule's name, description and create rules
with the body given, which has the same shape as the create call.
The rule keeps its ID, so its escalation chain, work-order rule and
past alarms stay attached to it. The change is applied immediately
and the updated rule is returned. When the body has no clearRule,
the rule's current clear rule, if any, is kept. A rule that is still
provisioning, has failed or is being deleted cannot be edited.

get.summary: Search a workspace product by name
get.description:
Finds devices, locations, alarm rules, work orders and dashboards
whose name (or label, for devices and locations) contains the query,
case-insensitively. Hits come grouped in that order, names that start
with the query first, at most `limit` of each kind. Alarm rules are
only searched for a product admin, since only an admin can list them;
dashboards only include those the caller may open. A query shorter
than 2 characters returns no hits; one longer than 100 is cut to 100.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most hits of each kind, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

get.description:
Returns one page of the work orders of the workspace product. Every filter is
optional and they combine. status may be given more than once, or as a
comma-separated list, to match any of them. Pagination is one-based; size is
clamped to 1-100.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only orders in one of these statuses

parameters.name: assigneeUserId
parameters.description: Only orders assigned to this user

parameters.name: unassigned
parameters.description: Only orders nobody is assigned to

parameters.name: assignedTeam
parameters.description: Only orders of this team, whatever the letter case

parameters.name: alarmId
parameters.description: Only orders raised for this alarm, open or closed

parameters.name: overdue
parameters.description: Only orders past their due time that are still OPEN, IN_PROGRESS or ON_HOLD

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text to find in the title or the equipment name, case-insensitive

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: PRIORITY is most urgent first; DUE is soonest due first, orders with no due time last

post.description:
Raises a work order in the workspace product. deviceId and assetId, when given,
must belong to that workspace product, and assigneeUserId must be an active
member of the workspace. status defaults to OPEN and source to MANUAL. An alarm
(alarmId) has at most one order that is OPEN, IN_PROGRESS or ON_HOLD.

example.title: Inspect the bearing of feed pump P-101
example.description: Vibration has been above 6 mm/s for an hour.

400.description: Invalid field, or a device, asset or assignee outside this workspace

409.description: The alarm already has a work order in hand

get.description:
Returns the work orders of the workspace product counted: by status; overdue;
unassigned and mine; and, over the last 30 days, how many were raised, how many
finished, how many of those met or missed their due time, and the average hours
from raised to finished.

post.summary: Change or delete several work orders
post.description:
Applies one change to each of the orders in ids (1 to 200). Of status, priority,
assigneeUserId, unassign and assignedTeam, the ones given are set and the rest
are left as they are on each order. delete true deletes the orders instead.
Each order is changed as a single update would change it. An order that cannot
be changed does not stop the rest: its ID comes back in failed.

200.description: Applied; succeeded and failed list the order IDs

400.description: No ids, more than 200, or nothing to change

put.description:
Replaces every editable field of the order; a field left null is cleared. Moving
the order to DONE or CANCELLED stamps closedAt, and moving it back clears it.
holdReason is kept only while status is ON_HOLD. What raised the order (source,
alarmId, externalRef) cannot be changed. Moving an order that has an alarmId and
a deviceId to DONE also acknowledges that alarm.

example.title: Inspect the bearing of feed pump P-101
example.description: Vibration has been above 6 mm/s for an hour.

400.description: Invalid field, or a device, asset or assignee outside this workspace

409.description: Reopening would give the alarm a second work order in hand

delete.description: Deletes the order and its history.

get.description:
Returns what happened to the order, oldest first: CREATED, STATUS_CHANGED,
ASSIGNED, UPDATED, NOTE and REPEATED (the alarm rule that raised the order fired
again on the device; toValue is the count so far).

post.summary: Add a note to a work order

example.note: Bearing replaced; vibration back to 2.1 mm/s.

get.summary: Get an alarm rule's work-order setting

404.description: Alarm rule not found, or it does not raise work orders

put.summary: Make an alarm rule raise work orders
put.description:
Creates or replaces the setting that raises a work order when the alarm rule
fires. Four limits keep a busy rule from flooding the list, checked in this
order: minSeverity, mergeRepeats, cooldownMinutes and dailyLimit.

400.description: Invalid field, or an assignee outside this workspace

delete.summary: Stop an alarm rule raising work orders
delete.description: Removes the setting. Orders already raised stay.

get.description: Returns the order's tasks in the order they are to be done.

put.description:
Makes the order's tasks the given list (at most 50), in that order. A task sent
with the id of one the order already has is kept, with what was done on it; a
task without an id is added; the ones left out are removed.

200.description: The order's tasks as they now are

put.description:
Marks one task of the order done, by the caller and now, or not done. An order
cannot be moved to DONE while a required task is not done.

200.description: Task returned as it now is

404.description: Work order or task not found

get.description: Returns the templates of the workspace product by name, each with its tasks in order.

post.description:
A template is a named list of tasks (at most 50). A work order raised with it
gets a copy of those tasks, so changing or deleting the template later leaves
orders already raised as they are.

example.name: High temperature
example.description: For a cooling loop running hot

put.description: Replaces the template's name, description and whole task list. Orders already raised with it are not changed.

example.name: High temperature
example.description: For a cooling loop running hot

delete.description: Orders already raised with it keep their tasks. An alarm rule that used it goes on raising orders, without tasks.
